meta.title: 2-3-2-3 In Possession · 20 Rondos & Exercises
meta.notes:
A complete in-possession programme for a 2-3-2-3 structure in the De Zerbi style: bait the press with the goalkeeper and centre-backs, find the free 6 and the third man, receive between the lines with the 8 and 10, and isolate the wingers.

Every slide has its own notes: tap the current slide number (or open Board menu, Slide notes and contents). On a large screen the notes sit beside the pitch.

Blocks: A rondos 01-06, B positional games 07-10, C patterns 11-14, D phases of play 15-18, E games 19-20.

items.text:
2-3-2-3 IN POSSESSION
20 rondos and exercises in the De Zerbi
style: bait the press, find the third
man, isolate the winger.

steps.title: 00 How to use this manual — Cover
steps.note:
Organisation:
- One board, 20 exercises, every slide animated. Press play, or switch Playback to “Tap for each slide” and talk the group through each picture.
- Every exercise opens with a set-up slide (area, numbers, rules, scoring), then the key actions one at a time, then coaching points and progressions.
- Slide titles group the slides by exercise: tap the current slide number to open the contents and jump straight to any exercise.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
- Pick one rondo (01-06) as the warm-up, one positional game (07-10), one pattern or phase (11-18) and finish with a game (19-20).
- A 90-minute session: warm-up rondo 15 min, positional game 20 min, pattern or phase 25 min, game 25 min, cool-down 5 min.

items.text: THE 2
THE 3
THE 2
THE 3

OUR 2-3-2-3
GK + 2 build, 3
protect and connect, 2
receive between lines,
3 pin the back line.

steps.title: 00 Our 2-3-2-3 — The structure
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 2: the centre-backs, split wide enough for the goalkeeper to play between them. The goalkeeper is the third player in the first line.
- 3: the fullbacks step inside beside the 6, forming the first midfield line. They protect the centre when we lose the ball.
- 2: the 8 and the 10 live in the half-spaces, between the opponent’s midfield and defence. They receive on the half-turn.
- 3: the wingers hold the touchline, high and wide, to pin the opposing fullbacks. The 9 pins both centre-backs.

Coaching points:
- Lines stay staggered: nobody in the same lane or at the same height as the teammate in front.
- Every player on the ball has a short option, a forward option and a switch.
- Bodies half-turned: a player with a man on his back sets first time on an angle; a player who is free and side-on plays forward.
- Rest defence is built in: the 2 + 3 behind the ball are five players ready to counter-press.

items.text:
BAIT THE PRESS
Stop the ball. Make
them come. Play into
the space they leave.

steps.title: 00 Our 2-3-2-3 — Principle 1: bait the press
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper keeps the ball still under his sole. The opponent’s front two must decide: press now, or let us build.

Coaching points:
- The pause is a question, not a delay: hold it only while a pass into the 6 or a centre-back remains available.
- The moment one presser commits, the space he left is our exit.

items.text:
FIND THE THIRD MAN
GK into the 6, who
bounces it first time
to the LCB. The LCB
faces forward.

steps.title: 00 Our 2-3-2-3 — Principle 2: find the third man
steps.note:
What happens:
Their striker jumped the goalkeeper, and his curved run blocks the pass to the left centre-back. The goalkeeper plays into the 6. Their 8 jumps onto the 6’s back as the ball travels. The 6 does not turn: he bounces it first time, on an angle, to the left centre-back, who now faces the pitch.

Coaching points:
- Third man: A cannot reach C, so A plays B and B sets C first time. The shape is a V or a zigzag, never a straight line through B.
- The 6 shows half-turned and sets with the foot away from the presser. One touch, because the press arrives with the ball.
- The left centre-back steps out of the striker’s shadow as the first pass travels, so the angle for the set is open.
- Never ask the 6 to receive from the goalkeeper and play forward past the man on his back.

items.text:
INTO THE SPACE HE LEFT
Their 8 jumped the 6:
the LCB plays our 8
between the lines.

steps.title: 00 Our 2-3-2-3 — Principle 2: play into the space he left
steps.note:
What happens:
Their 8 left his zone to press the 6. The left centre-back, facing forward, plays into our 8 in the space behind him, between their lines.

Coaching points:
- The presser who jumps opens a lane. The third man plays into it at once, before their midfield recovers.
- The 8 waits behind the midfielder and moves as the set is played, so he receives on the half-turn, already facing forward.

items.text:
ISOLATE THE WINGER
Draw them to one side,
switch to the 1v1.

steps.title: 00 Our 2-3-2-3 — Principle 3: isolate the winger
steps.note:
What happens:
The 8 has the ball facing forward with the block pulled to our left. The switch finds the right winger alone against his fullback.

Coaching points:
- Overload one side to isolate the other: four or five of ours draw the block, the winger waits wide and high.
- The 8 opens his body as the ball arrives, so the switch needs no extra touch.
- The winger receives on the half-turn, already facing his defender, and attacks at speed.
- The 9 attacks the near post, the 10 arrives for the cutback, the far winger attacks the back post.

steps.title: 00 Contents — The 20 exercises
steps.note:
Organisation:
- A · Rondos 01-06: the technical and decision habits (bait, third man, split, scan, switch, build with the goalkeeper).
- B · Positional games 07-10: the same habits inside zones that mirror our lines.
- C · Patterns 11-14: our four rehearsed routes, unopposed first, then against passive and live pressure.
- D · Phases of play 15-18: build-up against two pressing systems, progression through a mid-block, the final third.
- E · Games 19-20: rest defence and counter-press, then the full 11v11 game with bonus goals for our principles.

Dose:
- Rondos: 4-6 bouts of 90 s, 30 s rest. Positional games: 4 x 4 min, 1 min rest. Patterns: 8-10 reps each side, then opposed.
- Phases: 3 x 6 min. Games: 2 x 10 min. Adjust to age, fitness and the week’s load.

items.text:
01 · RONDO 4v1
Bait & release. 10 x
10 m, 2 touches.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 10 x 10 m square (8 x 8 m for a sharp group). Four attackers on the sides, one defender inside. Spare balls at every corner.
- Groups of five. 4-6 bouts of 90 seconds, 30 seconds rest.

Rules:
- Attackers stay on their line but can slide along it. Two touches maximum.
- The player on the ball may stop it under his sole (the bait). Once the defender commits, he has two seconds to pass.
- Defender wins the ball or forces it out: he swaps with the player who lost it.

Scoring:
- 10 passes in a row: 1 point.
- Bait pass, played after the defender has committed within 2 m: 2 points.
- Defender: 1 point per touch.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Our goalkeeper and centre-backs bait the first press in every build-up. This is the habit, five metres at a time.

items.text:
BAIT
Stop the ball under
the sole. Make the
defender come.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Bait: stop the ball
steps.note:
What happens:
Player 1 stops the ball under his sole and waits. The defender is invited to come and press.

Coaching points:
- Ball under the sole, body open to the inside of the square.
- Eyes up: check where 2 and 4 are before the defender arrives.
- Hold the pause only while a pass is still on.

items.text:
RELEASE
Play into the side he
left. Bait pass = 2
points.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Release to the side he left
steps.note:
What happens:
The defender has committed from the top. Player 1 releases into the side he left: player 2 at the bottom.

Coaching points:
- Release as he commits, not after he arrives.
- Weight the pass to the receiver’s far foot so he can open up.
- Bait pass scores 2 points.

items.text:
BACK FOOT
Receive across the
body, already facing
the next pass.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Receive on the back foot, bait again
steps.note:
What happens:
Player 2 receives across his body on the back foot and is already facing player 3. The defender recovers towards him.

Coaching points:
- Open body before the ball arrives: hips facing the next pass, not the passer.
- First touch out of the defender’s path.
- If the defender comes again, bait again.

items.text:
READ THE SHADOW
Never pass into the
lane his body covers.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Read the shadow
steps.note:
What happens:
The defender presses player 2 from the left, so his shadow covers the pass back to 1. Player 2 plays away from the shadow, to 3.

Coaching points:
- Look at the defender’s body: the lane behind him is closed, every other lane is open.
- Do not force the pass he is protecting.
- Ask: where is his shadow? Where is the free pass?

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Scan · open body ·
pause with a purpose ·
release into his
space.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Scan before the ball arrives: know the free pass before you receive.
- Open body on the back foot.
- The pause is a weapon only when a pass is still on.
- Release into the space the presser left.
- Two touches: control away from pressure, then pass.

Questions to ask:
- Why did you stop the ball there?
- Which pass did the defender’s body close?
- Where did he come from, and so where is the space?

items.text:
PROGRESS
8 x 8 m · one touch
except the bait ·
second defender after
10 passes.

steps.title: 01 Rondo 4v1 · Bait & release — Progressions
steps.note:
Progressions:
- Shrink to 8 x 8 m.
- One touch, except the bait: the pause is the only time the ball may stop.
- Second defender enters after 10 passes (becomes 4v2).

Regressions:
- 12 x 12 m, three touches.
- Defender passive for the first 30 seconds.

Dose:
4-6 bouts of 90 s, 30 s rest. Rotate the defender every bout.

items.text:
02 · RONDO 5v2
Third-man square. 12
x 12 m, the 6
inside.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 12 x 12 m square. Four attackers on the sides, the 6 inside, two defenders inside.
- Groups of seven. 5 bouts of 2 minutes, 45 seconds rest.

Rules:
- Outside players: two touches. The 6: two touches, one touch when he sets the ball.
- Defenders win it: the two players responsible (the passer and the intended receiver) become defenders.

Scoring:
- Third man: outside → 6 → first-time set on an angle to another outside player, who plays the pass the first passer could not: 1 point.
- Split pass between the two defenders: 1 point.
- The 6 turns and plays to the opposite side, only when nobody is behind him: 2 points.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
The 6 in our 2-3-2-3 is the player the first press leaves free. This rondo teaches everyone to use him without asking him to turn into a man on his back.

items.text:
FIND THE POCKET
The 6 shows between
the defenders, half-
turned.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — The 6 finds the pocket
steps.note:
What happens:
Before the pass, the 6 moves into the pocket between the two defenders, on the ball’s side, and opens his body towards player 2.

Coaching points:
- Move to receive as the passer’s head goes down, not before.
- Show on an angle, half-turned, so you see the passer and player 2 at the same time.

items.text:
UP
Into the 6. Their
defender jumps his
back; player 2
slides.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — Up to the 6
steps.note:
What happens:
Player 3 is unreachable: the second defender’s shadow covers him. Player 1 plays up into the 6, and that defender jumps onto the 6’s back. Player 2 slides along his line towards the ball.

Coaching points:
- Pass into the 6’s foot away from the defender.
- Player 2 slides towards the ball as the pass travels: that slide makes the angle for the set.
- The 6 now has a man on his back: he will not turn.

items.text:
SET ON AN ANGLE
The 6 bounces it
first time to player
2: a V, not a
straight line.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — Set on an angle to the third man
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 bounces the ball first time, back on an angle, to player 2. The pass makes a V: in from player 1, out to player 2. Player 2 receives facing into the square.

Coaching points:
- First time: the set is quicker than the defender on his back.
- Third man: A cannot reach C, so A plays B and B sets C. The shape is a V, never a straight line through the 6.
- Set with the foot away from the defender, into player 2’s front foot.

items.text:
THIRD MAN · 1 POINT
Up to the 6, set to
2, out to 3.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — The pass player 1 could not make: 1 point
steps.note:
What happens:
Both defenders were drawn to the 6. Player 3 slides down his line and player 2, facing forward, finds him: the pass player 1 could not make. 1 point.

Coaching points:
- The third man plays forward with his first or second touch, before the defenders turn.
- Player 3 slides along his line to open the lane.
- Up, set, out: three passes, two of them first time.

items.text:
SPLIT · 1 POINT
Through the gap
between the two
defenders.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — Split the pair
steps.note:
What happens:
Both defenders shift to the ball. A gap opens between them: player 3 splits them with a pass straight back to player 1.

Coaching points:
- Look for the gap between the defenders before looking around them.
- A split pass is firm and on the ground.
- The 6 moves out of the passing line so he does not block it.

items.text:
TURN · 2 POINTS
Nobody behind him:
the 6 turns and
plays forward.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — The 6 turns when he is free
steps.note:
What happens:
This time both defenders are on the ball side and nobody is behind the 6. He receives on the half-turn and plays to the opposite side: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- Scan over the shoulder before receiving: is anyone behind me?
- Someone behind: set first time on an angle. Nobody behind: turn.
- The decision is made before the ball arrives.

items.text:
TURN · 2 POINTS
Open up across the
body and play
forward.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — The turn
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 opens up across his body, away from the defenders, and plays to player 3 on the opposite side.

Coaching points:
- Turn away from the nearest defender.
- Two touches: one to turn, one to pass.

items.text:
PROGRESS
5v3 · the 6 one
touch · outside one
touch after a set.

steps.title: 02 Rondo 5v2 · Third-man square — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The 6 scans twice before every pass he receives.
- A man on his back: set first time on an angle. Nobody behind: turn.
- Outside players slide along the line to give the set an angle.
- Set passes are first time; turns are with two touches.

Progressions:
- Add a third defender (5v3).
- The 6 must play one touch.
- Outside players one touch after a set from the 6.

Regressions:
- 15 x 15 m.
- Only one defender may press the 6.

Dose:
5 x 2 min, 45 s rest.

items.text:
03 · RONDO 4v2
Split & counter-press.
10 x 10 m, two escape
gates.

steps.title: 03 Rondo 4v2 · Split & counter-press — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 10 x 10 m square. Two 2 m pole gates in the middle of the top and bottom lines.
- Four attackers, two defenders. 6 bouts of 90 seconds, 30 seconds rest.

Rules:
- Attackers two touches. When the defenders win the ball they have 5 seconds to escape: pass or dribble through either gate.
- Attackers who lose the ball must win it back inside those 5 seconds.

Scoring:
- Split pass between the defenders: 2 points. 8 passes: 1 point.
- Regain inside 5 seconds: 2 points. Defenders escape through a gate: 2 points to them.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Counter-pressing is part of our possession. Our 2 + 3 behind the ball exist so that every loss is pressed at once.

items.text:
SPLIT · 2 POINTS
Through the gap
between the two
defenders.

steps.title: 03 Rondo 4v2 · Split & counter-press — Split pass: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The defenders leave a gap between them. Player 1 splits them with a firm pass to player 3.

Coaching points:
- Look through them first, around them second.
- Split passes are firm, along the ground, to the receiver’s far foot.

items.text:
LOST IT
The defender steps in
front of player 2.

steps.title: 03 Rondo 4v2 · Split & counter-press — The ball is lost
steps.note:
What happens:
Player 3 forces a pass to player 2. The second defender steps across and intercepts.

Coaching points:
- A loss is the trigger. Do not appeal, react.

items.text: 5 SECONDS

COUNTER-PRESS
Nearest two press, far
two close the gate and
the pass.

steps.title: 03 Rondo 4v2 · Split & counter-press — Counter-press: 5 seconds
steps.note:
What happens:
The two nearest attackers press the ball at once. The other two close the escape routes: one blocks the pass to the other defender, one guards the gate.

Coaching points:
- Nearest player presses the ball, second nearest closes the inside.
- The far players do not watch: they block a gate or the pass.
- Press to win the ball, not to make contact: arrive on the half-turn, ready to tackle.

items.text:
REGAIN · 2 POINTS
Won back inside 5
seconds. Secure it,
then rebuild.

steps.title: 03 Rondo 4v2 · Split & counter-press — Regain: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
Surrounded, the defender loses the ball inside 5 seconds. Attackers score 2 points and restart from the side lines.

Coaching points:
- After the regain, the first pass is safe: secure the ball, then rebuild the shape.

items.text:
PROGRESS
3-second regain · an
outside target for the
escape.

steps.title: 03 Rondo 4v2 · Split & counter-press — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Split first, around second.
- The loss is the trigger: nearest two press, far two cut the exits.
- Count the 5 seconds out loud so the group learns the rhythm.

Progressions:
- 3 seconds to regain.
- A third defender waits outside a gate and becomes a target for the escape pass.

Regressions:
- 12 x 12 m.
- Escape only by dribbling through a gate.

Dose:
6 x 90 s, 30 s rest.

items.text:
04 · BOX RONDO 6v3
Four outside, the 8
and 10 inside. 16 x
16 m.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 16 x 16 m. Four outside players (CB, 9, LW, RW), the 8 and the 10 inside, three defenders.
- Groups of nine. 5 bouts of 2 minutes, 1 minute rest.

Rules:
- Outside: two touches. Inside: two touches. Defenders win it: they swap with the passer and the two inside players rotate out.
- The 8 and the 10 must never stand in the same line or at the same height.

Scoring:
- Outside → inside → outside on the opposite side: 1 point.
- Outside → 8 → 10 → outside (the box connection): 2 points.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
The 8 and the 10 are the second line of our 2-3-2-3. They work as a pair between the lines, at different heights, always connected.

items.text:
STAGGER
The 8 and 10 never
share a line or a
height.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — Stagger the inside pair
steps.note:
What happens:
The 8 and the 10 stand at different heights and on different sides of the defenders, so one pass can never block the other.

Coaching points:
- Never in the same line: if the 8 is high, the 10 is low.
- Each inside player shows to a different outside player.
- Half-turned bodies: see the ball and the far side.

items.text:
INTO THE BOX
CB into the 8. The
10 moves to stay
connected.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — CB finds the 8
steps.note:
What happens:
The centre-back plays into the 8 between two defenders.

Coaching points:
- Pass into the 8’s far foot, away from the nearest defender.
- The 10 moves as the ball travels to stay connected to the 8.

items.text:
BOX CONNECTION
8 to 10 inside. The
9 slides to open the
lane.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — 8 to 10: the box connection
steps.note:
What happens:
The 8 finds the 10 inside: the defenders have to turn their backs on the outside players.

Coaching points:
- One-touch between the inside pair whenever possible.
- The 10 receives side-on, facing the far side, so his next pass needs no turn.
- The 9 slides along his line as the ball travels, out of the third defender’s shadow.

items.text:
OUT · 2 POINTS
CB → 8 → 10 → 9. Two
lines broken.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — Out the far side: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 received side-on, already facing the far side, so he plays out to the 9 without turning. Outside → 8 → 10 → outside: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- Play out to the side the defenders are not facing.
- The 9 receives on the back foot and restarts at once.

items.text:
FIND THE FREE SIDE
They shift to the
ball, the inside
pair rotate away.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — The defenders shift, find the free side
steps.note:
What happens:
The defenders shift towards the 9, the nearest one pressing him from the inside. The 9 plays away from him, down to the right winger, who has slid along his line. The inside pair rotate to the free side and the RW finds the 10, now facing the centre-back.

Coaching points:
- When the defenders shift, the inside pair shift the opposite way.
- Play away from the presser’s side: he comes from the inside, the ball goes round the outside.
- Keep a triangle with every pass: two options for the man on the ball.

items.text:
PROGRESS
6v4 · inside one
touch · only the box
connection scores.

steps.title: 04 Rondo 6v3 · Box rondo — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Stagger: different heights, different lanes.
- Inside-inside connections break two lines with one pass.
- Bodies half-turned, scan before receiving.
- When the block shifts, rotate away from it.

Progressions:
- Four defenders (6v4).
- Inside players one touch.
- Only the box connection (8 to 10) scores.

Regressions:
- 20 x 20 m.
- One inside player only (5v3).

Dose:
5 x 2 min, 1 min rest.

items.text:
05 · DOUBLE SQUARE
Draw them in,
switch through the
link player.

steps.title: 05 Rondo 9v2 · Double-square switch — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Two 10 x 10 m squares with a 10 x 6 m link zone between them. Four attackers around each square, a link player (L) in the link zone.
- Two defenders in each square. Only the two in the square with the ball may press. 4 bouts of 3 minutes, 1 minute rest.

Rules:
- Attackers two touches. After at least three passes in a square, the ball may be switched through the link player.
- The link player is fed by a side player of the square (top or bottom), never by the player whose back is to him.
- He receives side-on and plays into the top or bottom player of the other square with his first or second touch.
- Defenders win it: they swap with the two attackers who lost it.

Scoring:
- Switch completed (square → link → other square): 2 points.
- Direct pass from square to square, skipping the link: not allowed.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
We draw the opponent to one side, then switch through a central player. The link player is our 6.

items.text:
DRAW THEM IN
Round square A
until both
defenders are on
the left.

steps.title: 05 Rondo 9v2 · Double-square switch — Circulate to draw them in
steps.note:
What happens:
Three quick passes round square A, 3 to 2 to 1 to 4, pull both defenders across to the left of the square, away from the link.

Coaching points:
- Patience: the switch only works if the defenders are drawn.
- Quick, firm passes to the next player along; each receiver is on the back foot, already facing the next pass.

items.text:
INTO THE LINK
Player 4 plays
away from the
presser; the link
shows half-turned.

steps.title: 05 Rondo 9v2 · Double-square switch — Into the link player
steps.note:
What happens:
The first defender presses player 4 from the left. Player 4 is side-on, so he plays away from the presser, across his body, into the link player, who has shown half-turned to see both squares.

Coaching points:
- Feed the link from the side of the square: player 4 faces the link side-on, player 3 would have his back to it.
- Link player: show on an angle, open to the other square, never square to the passer.
- Pass into his front foot so he can play on with the next touch.

items.text:
SWITCH · 2 POINTS
Square A → link →
top of square B.

steps.title: 05 Rondo 9v2 · Double-square switch — Switch: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
Nobody may press the link player, so he receives side-on and plays into the top player of square B, who also stands side-on to him. Square A → link → square B: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- Free and side-on: he can play on with his first or second touch. If a defender may enter the zone (progression), he sets back first time instead.
- Play into the side player of square B, never into player 5, whose back is to the link.

items.text:
SQUARE B LIVE
Their defenders
press; ours set
away from them and
restart the count.

steps.title: 05 Rondo 9v2 · Double-square switch — Square B is live
steps.note:
What happens:
The two defenders in square B press at once, the first from the right. Player 8 bounces the ball first time, back on an angle, to player 5, away from the presser. The defenders in square A stop and the count restarts.

Coaching points:
- Receive the switch on the back foot and play away from the first presser.
- A man arriving on you: set first time on an angle, do not turn.
- The link player resets to the middle of his zone.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A defender may
enter the link
zone · link player
one touch.

steps.title: 05 Rondo 9v2 · Double-square switch — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Draw before you switch.
- The link player is half-turned before the ball arrives.
- Firm passes: the switch must be faster than the defenders.

Progressions:
- A defender may enter the link zone after the third pass: the link player must now set first time.
- Link player one touch.
- Count only switches made within 8 seconds of entering a square.

Regressions:
- Link zone 10 x 10 m.
- Two passes before a switch instead of three.

Dose:
4 x 3 min, 1 min rest.

items.text:
06 · GK BUILD RONDO
GK + LCB + RCB + 6 v
2. Out through the
gates.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Penalty area extended to 30 m, width of the box (42 m). Two 6 m pole gates on the 30 m line, one in each half-space.
- GK, LCB, RCB and the 6 against two pressers. The 8 and the 10 wait beyond the gates as targets.
- 4 bouts of 3 minutes. Restart every attack from the goalkeeper.

Rules:
- Pressers win it: they try to score in the big goal within 6 seconds.
- Two touches for outfield players, free for the goalkeeper.
- The targets cannot enter the area; they move along the line to show through a gate.

Scoring:
- Pass through a gate to the 8 or 10: 1 point.
- Through a gate after a bait (a presser committed to the man on the ball): 2 points.
- Pressers: goal 2 points.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
This is the first line of our 2-3-2-3 against a front two: goalkeeper plus two centre-backs, with the 6 as the free man.

items.text:
BAIT
GK to LCB. Stop the
ball, invite the first
presser.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — Goalkeeper to LCB: bait
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper plays to the left centre-back, who stops the ball under his sole. The first presser is invited.

Coaching points:
- Centre-backs start wide, at the edge of the box, so the goalkeeper has an angle.
- Bait with the ball on the side away from the presser.
- The presser comes from the front and outside: the lane inside, into the 6, stays open.

items.text:
3 v 1 BEHIND HIM
GK, RCB and 6 against
one presser. Someone
is free.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — The second presser must choose
steps.note:
What happens:
The first presser has committed to the left centre-back. The second presser must now choose: screen the 6, or jump the right centre-back. He cannot do both.

Coaching points:
- Count: three of us (GK, RCB, 6) against one presser. One of us is free.
- The 6 moves to stay out of the second presser’s shadow.

items.text:
FREE MAN
The second presser
chose the RCB: the 6
is free.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — Into the 6
steps.note:
What happens:
The second presser screened the right centre-back, so the 6 is free between them. The left centre-back plays into the 6.

Coaching points:
- Play into the free man the moment he is free; do not wait for him to wave.
- The 6 receives half-turned, facing the gates.

items.text:
THROUGH · 2 POINTS
Free and side-on, the
6 plays on through the
gate.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — Through the gate: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
Nobody is within 10 m of the 6, so he does not need to set: he receives side-on, across his body, and plays on through the right gate into the 10. Through a gate after a bait: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- Scan before the ball arrives: a presser on your back means set first time on an angle; nobody near means receive across the body and play on.
- The 10 shows late through the gate, on the side away from the nearest presser.
- Pass and support: the 6 follows the ball for the next action.

items.text:
GO DIRECT
6 marked: the RCB
carries and passes
through the gate.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — If the 6 is marked: go direct
steps.note:
What happens:
The second presser now marks the 6. The right centre-back is free and plays directly through the right gate.

Coaching points:
- If the 6 is marked, the centre-back is free: carry forward until someone stops you, then pass.
- Through, around or over: take the quickest safe exit.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A third presser after
the first pass · gates
4 m.

steps.title: 06 GK build rondo · GK + 3 v 2 — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Centre-backs wide, goalkeeper as the third man in the line.
- Bait one presser to free a teammate.
- Count the numbers behind the first presser.
- The 6 lives outside the second presser’s shadow.

Progressions:
- A third presser (their 8) joins from the 30 m line after the first pass: 4 v 3.
- Goalkeeper two touches.
- Gates 4 m wide.

Regressions:
- One presser only for the first bout.
- Gates 8 m wide.

Dose:
4 x 3 min, 1 min rest. Switch the goalkeeper every bout if you have two.

items.text:
07 · UP-BACK-THROUGH
Three zones: 3 v 1, 2
v 2, 1 v 1. Up to the
9, back to a facing 8,
through.

steps.title: 07 Positional game · Up-back-through — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 36 x 24 m split into three 12 m zones. Zone 1: LCB, 6 and RCB against one presser. Zone 2: the 8 and 10 against two. Zone 3: the 9 against one defender.
- Players stay in their zones. 4 bouts of 4 minutes, 1 minute rest. Spare balls with the coach behind zone 1.

Rules:
- Two touches. A pass may not skip zone 2 except the “up” pass into the 9.
- Defenders win it: they play to the coach and the attack restarts from zone 1.

Scoring:
- Up-back-through completed (zone 1 → 9 → set to zone 2 → through into zone 3): 2 points.
- Zone 1 → zone 2 → zone 3 without the set: 1 point.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
The 6 plays up to the 9, the 9 sets back to a facing 8 or 10, who plays through. It is how our second line receives facing forward without turning under pressure.

items.text:
UP
The 9 drops off his
marker. The 6 plays
into his feet.

steps.title: 07 Positional game · Up-back-through — Up: the 6 finds the 9
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 drops towards the ball and the 6 plays the up pass past the zone 2 defenders straight into his feet.

Coaching points:
- The 9 shows on the side away from his marker, body half-open.
- Firm pass into the 9’s back foot.
- The 8 and 10 move as the ball travels, to be facing the 9.

items.text:
BACK
The 9 sets first time
to the 8 arriving
facing forward.

steps.title: 07 Positional game · Up-back-through — Back: set to the facing 8
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 is marked from behind, so he sets first time back to the 8, who arrived facing forward.

Coaching points:
- The 9 never turns into his marker: set and spin.
- The 8 arrives late and receives on the move, already facing zone 3.

items.text:
THROUGH · 2 POINTS
The 10 runs beyond,
the 8 plays into his
path.

steps.title: 07 Positional game · Up-back-through — Through: the 10 runs beyond
steps.note:
What happens:
As the 8 receives, the 10 runs past the zone 3 defender, who is drawn to the 9. The 8 plays through into the 10’s path: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- The runner goes as the set pass travels, not after.
- Pass into space in front of the runner, not to his feet.
- The 9 spins the other way to drag his defender.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Up to the man who can
set · back to the man
facing · through into
the run.

steps.title: 07 Positional game · Up-back-through — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Up: the forward pass goes into the player who can set, not the one who must turn.
- Back: first-time set to a teammate who is already facing forward.
- Through: the run starts as the set travels; the pass goes into space.
- Zone 1: three against one means one of you is always free. Find him.

Questions to ask:
- Who could see the 10’s run when the 9 received?
- Why did the 9 set instead of turning?

items.text:
PROGRESS
Defenders may follow
into zone 3 · first-
time through ball ·
add a goal.

steps.title: 07 Positional game · Up-back-through — Progressions
steps.note:
Progressions:
- A zone 2 defender may follow his man into zone 3.
- The through pass must be first time.
- Add a goal and goalkeeper at the end of zone 3: finish the move.

Regressions:
- Zone 2 defenders passive.
- Three touches.

Dose:
4 x 4 min, 1 min rest. Rotate the zones every bout.

items.text:
08 · 4v4 + 3
Find the free man.
End to end through
the 6 = 2 points.

steps.title: 08 Positional game 4v4+3 · Find the free man — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 30 x 25 m. Blue 4 v red 4 inside, plus three neutrals: one on each end line (J) and one central (the 6).
- Neutrals always play with the team in possession. 4 bouts of 4 minutes, 1 minute rest.

Rules:
- Two touches for everyone; the central 6 one touch when he sets.
- End neutrals may move along their line; they cannot pass to each other directly.

Scoring:
- End to end (one end neutral to the other): 1 point.
- End to end through the central 6, who sets first time on an angle to a blue player facing forward (third man): 2 points.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
The central neutral is our 6: always free in the first line. The blue players inside are the 8, 10 and the fullbacks who step into midfield.

items.text:
THE FREE 6
He moves off the red
players; the end
neutral finds him.

steps.title: 08 Positional game 4v4+3 · Find the free man — Into the free 6
steps.note:
What happens:
The central 6 moves off the red players into the free space between them, half-turned, and the end neutral plays into him.

Coaching points:
- The 6 is always the free man: if he is marked, someone else is free.
- Show half-turned, seeing the passer and the blue players on your side.

items.text:
THIRD MAN
Two press the 6: he
sets first time to
the 8 facing
forward.

steps.title: 08 Positional game 4v4+3 · Find the free man — Set back to the 8: the third man
steps.note:
What happens:
Two red players squeeze the 6, one on his back. He does not turn: he bounces the ball first time, back on an angle, to the 8, who has stepped into the space they left and now faces the far end.

Coaching points:
- A man on your back: set first time on an angle. The shape is a V: in from the end neutral, out to the 8.
- The 8 moves as the first pass travels, away from his marker, so he receives facing forward.
- Third man: the end neutral could not reach the 8; the 6 could.

items.text:
2 POINTS
J → 6 → set to the 8
→ J. The red block
is broken.

steps.title: 08 Positional game 4v4+3 · Find the free man — End to end through the third man: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The 8 faces the far end with the red players drawn to the 6. He plays the far end neutral first time: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- The third man plays forward at once, before the red players turn.
- The end neutral moves along his line to open the angle.

items.text:
TURNOVER
Red win it: the
neutrals play for
red. Blue press for
5 seconds.

steps.title: 08 Positional game 4v4+3 · Find the free man — Turnover: the neutrals change sides
steps.note:
What happens:
If red win the ball, the three neutrals play for red. Blue counter-press for 5 seconds before re-forming the shape.

Coaching points:
- On a loss, the nearest two press and the rest block the central 6.
- The neutrals switch instantly; there is no pause.

items.text:
PROGRESS
6 one touch · under
6 passes · 5 red v 4
blue.

steps.title: 08 Positional game 4v4+3 · Find the free man — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Always one free man: find him with your first look.
- Third man: if you cannot reach him, play the man who can, and he sets first time on an angle.
- A man on your back: set. Nobody behind you: turn.
- Width and depth from the blue players; the 6 gives the centre.

Progressions:
- The central 6 one touch always.
- Points only if the end-to-end move takes fewer than 6 passes.
- Five red against four blue.

Regressions:
- 35 x 30 m.
- Three touches.

Dose:
4 x 4 min, 1 min rest.

items.text:
09 · HALF-SPACE BOX 6v4
Find the 8 or 10 in
the corridors behind
the red box.

steps.title: 09 Positional game 6v4 · Half-space box — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 40 x 34 m. Two 20 x 7 m half-space corridors (blue) and a 5 m end zone for the 9 (orange).
- Blue: LB, 6 and RB on the base, the 8 and 10 in the half-spaces, the 9 in the end zone. Red: four midfielders in a box.
- 4 bouts of 4 minutes, 1 minute rest.

Rules:
- Base players may not enter the corridors. Only the 8 and 10 may receive in a corridor. The 9 stays in the end zone.
- Red win it: they score by passing through the base line (any gap between the cones).

Scoring:
- 8 or 10 receives in a corridor and plays into the 9: 1 point.
- Receives in a corridor facing forward (on the half-turn) and plays the 9 first time: 2 points.
- 9 sets back to an arriving 8 or 10 who shoots or dribbles into the end zone: +1.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
The 8 and 10 are the “2” of our 2-3-2-3: they live in the half-spaces, behind the opponent’s midfield, and receive on the half-turn.

items.text:
MOVE THE BOX
6 to RB. The red box
slides to the ball.

steps.title: 09 Positional game 6v4 · Half-space box — Circulate to move the box
steps.note:
What happens:
The base circulates: 6 to RB. The red box slides across to the ball.

Coaching points:
- Quick ball on the base pulls the red box sideways.
- Look inside after every pass: the corridor behind them opens as they move.

items.text:
INTO THE CORRIDOR
The box went right;
the 8 is free on the
left.

steps.title: 09 Positional game 6v4 · Half-space box — The far corridor opens: RB to the 8
steps.note:
What happens:
With the box on the right, the 8’s corridor is open. The right-back plays the diagonal through the box into the 8.

Coaching points:
- The 8 holds his position behind the red midfielders until the ball can reach him.
- Diagonal passes break the box; square passes feed it.

items.text:
HALF-TURN · 2 POINTS
Facing forward,
first time into the
9.

steps.title: 09 Positional game 6v4 · Half-space box — Half-turn and play the 9: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
Nobody is within 9 m of the 8, so he receives on the half-turn, across his body, already facing forward, and plays the 9 first time: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- Back foot, open hips, already facing the 9 as the ball arrives.
- The 10 moves inside to support the next action.

items.text:
SET AND ARRIVE · +1
The 9 sets, the 10
drives into the end
zone.

steps.title: 09 Positional game 6v4 · Half-space box — Set to the arriving 10: +1
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 sets back to the 10, who arrives from the far corridor and drives into the end zone: +1.

Coaching points:
- The 9 sets to the player facing, not the closest player.
- The 10 arrives at speed, from behind the ball.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A defender guards
the end zone · two
touches in the
corridors.

steps.title: 09 Positional game 6v4 · Half-space box — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Move the box with quick base circulation, then play through it.
- Corridor players: behind the midfielders, never level with them.
- Receive on the half-turn: see the 9 and the ball at the same time.
- Diagonal passes break the box; square ones feed it.

Progressions:
- A fifth red defender in front of the end zone.
- Corridor players two touches maximum.
- The base may only make three passes before going forward.

Regressions:
- Corridors 9 m wide.
- Red pressers passive for the first minute.

Dose:
4 x 4 min, 1 min rest.

items.text:
10 · OVERLOAD TO ISOLATE
Draw them to one
side, switch, win
the 1v1.

steps.title: 10 Positional game · Overload to isolate — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 56 x 56 m with a 7 m wide channel on each side. Blue: LB, 6, RB, 8, 10, 9 inside, a winger in each channel. Red: six inside plus a fullback for each channel.
- Wingers stay in their channels. A red fullback may enter his channel only when the ball is played into it. 4 bouts of 5 minutes.

Rules:
- Two touches inside, unlimited in the channels.
- Red win it: they score by dribbling over our end line.

Scoring:
- Four passes on one half of the pitch, then a switch to the far winger: 1 point.
- Winger beats his fullback 1v1 and crosses or dribbles over the end line: 2 more points.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Our wingers hold the touchline, high and wide, while the ball is on the other side. The more players we draw to one side, the bigger the 1v1 on the other.

items.text:
OVERLOAD LEFT
Four passes on the
left, every set on
an angle. Red
slide over. RW
stays wide.

steps.title: 10 Positional game · Overload to isolate — Overload the left
steps.note:
What happens:
Four passes on the left: LB up the line to the LW, who sets first time back to the LB; LB into the 8, who checks to the ball and sets first time to the 6. Every set is on an angle, so the 6 receives already facing the right. Red slide over to the ball.

Coaching points:
- Short, quick passes: make the overload look dangerous so they commit to it.
- A man on your back: set first time on an angle (the LW, the 8). Facing forward: play forward (the LB).
- The 6 receives from the 8 already facing the far side: the switch needs no turn.
- The right winger stays wide and high. He does not come to the ball.

items.text:
SWITCH · 1 POINT
The 6 finds the
right winger, now
1v1.

steps.title: 10 Positional game · Overload to isolate — Switch to the isolated winger: 1 point
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 received from the 8 already facing the right. He switches to the right winger, now alone against his fullback.

Coaching points:
- The switch is driven, in the air or along the ground, to the winger’s far foot.
- The winger receives on the half-turn, already facing his defender.

items.text:
1v1 · 2 POINTS
At the defender,
change pace, to
the end line.

steps.title: 10 Positional game · Overload to isolate — Win the 1v1: 2 more points
steps.note:
What happens:
The fullback enters the channel. The winger attacks him at speed and drives to the end line.

Coaching points:
- First touch forward, at the defender.
- Change of pace past him; protect the ball with the body.
- The 9 and 10 attack the box for the cross.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A second defender
after 3 s · one-
pass switch ·
finish on goal.

steps.title: 10 Positional game · Overload to isolate — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Draw first: the switch only works when the block has shifted.
- Far winger: wide, high, patient. Never come to the ball.
- Switch to the far foot, with pace.
- 1v1: attack the defender’s front foot and change pace.

Progressions:
- A second red defender may join the channel after 3 seconds.
- The switch must be one pass.
- Finish on a goal with a goalkeeper.

Regressions:
- Channels 10 m wide.
- Fullbacks passive until the winger’s first touch.

Dose:
4 x 5 min, 1 min 30 rest.

items.text:
11 · BAIT & THIRD MAN
GK → 6 → bounce to LCB
→ 8 → LW in behind →
cutback.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Full pitch, our 2-3-2-3 in position. Four passive players as their front two and two central midfielders: they jog to their pressing trigger but do not tackle.
- Run the pattern on the left, then mirror it on the right. 8-10 reps each side, then the opposed version (last slide).

Rules:
- Every pass on the coach’s rhythm at first, then at match speed.
- Each rep ends with a finish on goal.

What happens:
GK holds (bait) → their striker jumps → GK into the 6 → their 8 jumps the 6 → the 6 bounces first time to the LCB (third man) → LCB into the 8 → LW in behind → cutback.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
This is our main exit from the first press: bait with the goalkeeper, use the 6 as the wall, find the centre-back facing forward, play into the space the jumping midfielder left.

items.text:
1 · BAIT
GK holds. Their
striker jumps and
blocks the LCB.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — 1 · Bait: the goalkeeper holds the ball
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper stops the ball under his sole. Their striker jumps him, curving his run so his shadow blocks the pass to the left centre-back.

Coaching points:
- The pause is a question: hold it until a presser commits.
- The striker’s curve tells us which pass he closed: the LCB is shut, so the 6 and the third man are the way out.

items.text:
2 · INTO THE 6
The 6 drops, the GK
plays him, their 8
jumps his back.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — 2 · Into the 6: their 8 jumps
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 drops into the gap between their strikers, half-turned, and the goalkeeper plays into him. Their 8 jumps onto the 6’s back as the ball travels.

Coaching points:
- The 6 shows late, between the strikers, with his body open to the left centre-back.
- Goalkeeper: firm pass into the 6’s left foot, the foot away from the presser.
- The 6 knows before the ball arrives: a man on my back, so I set; I do not turn.

items.text:
3 · THIRD MAN
The 6 bounces it first
time to the LCB, who
faces forward.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — 3 · Bounce to the LCB: third man
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 bounces the ball first time, back on an angle, to the left centre-back. The goalkeeper could not reach him; the 6 could. The left centre-back receives facing forward, and nobody is near him.

Coaching points:
- First time: one touch, with the foot away from the presser. The shape is a V: in from the goalkeeper, out to the LCB.
- The left centre-back steps out of the striker’s shadow as the first pass travels, so the angle is open.
- Third man: A cannot reach C, so A plays B and B sets C.

items.text:
4 · INTO THE SPACE
Their 8 jumped: the
LCB plays our 8
between the lines.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — 4 · Into the space their 8 left
steps.note:
What happens:
Their 8 jumped the 6, so our 8 is free behind him. The left centre-back plays straight into the 8, who receives on the half-turn in the left half-space, already facing forward.

Coaching points:
- The presser who jumps opens the lane: play into it at once, before he recovers.
- The 8 waits behind their midfielder and moves as the set is played.
- Firm pass into the 8’s back foot so he can open up with the first touch.

items.text:
5 · IN BEHIND
LW runs outside-in;
the 8 plays into his
path.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — 5 · Through to the LW
steps.note:
What happens:
The left winger runs from wide into the channel between fullback and centre-back. The 8, free and facing forward, plays through into his path.

Coaching points:
- The run starts as the 8 receives, from outside to inside.
- Pass into space ahead of the runner, weighted so he can take it in stride.
- The 9 pins the centre-back by moving the other way.

items.text:
6 · CUTBACK
9 near post, 10
penalty spot, RW far
post, 8 the edge.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — 6 · Cutback and arrivals
steps.note:
What happens:
The winger drives towards the byline and cuts back. The 9 attacks the near post, the 10 arrives at the penalty spot, the RW attacks the far post, the 8 follows to the edge of the box.

Coaching points:
- Cutback along the ground, behind the defenders running back.
- Arrive, do not wait: each runner has a lane.
- Finish first time.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Bait · first-time
bounce on an angle ·
third man faces
forward · play into
the space.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Bait: the pause lasts until a presser commits, then the ball moves at once.
- The 6 shows late between the strikers and bounces first time on an angle; he never turns into the man on his back.
- The third man (LCB) faces forward and plays into the space the jumping midfielder left.
- The 8 receives on the half-turn: one look, one touch, one pass.
- Runs start as the pass before travels, from outside to inside.
- Arrivals: near post, penalty spot, far post, edge of the box.

Questions to ask:
- Which pass did the striker’s curve close?
- Who was free when their 8 jumped the 6?
- Why did the 6 bounce it instead of turning?

items.text:
OPPOSED
Live pressers, back
four and goalkeeper.
Read the free man.

steps.title: 11 Pattern · Bait & third man — Opposed: live front four, back four and goalkeeper
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Make the four pressers live, add a back four and a goalkeeper.
- Pressers start passive for 3 reps, then live.

Rules:
- If the pressers win the ball they attack our goal; we counter-press for 5 seconds.
- The pattern is the plan; the pressers decide whether it is on.

Scoring:
- Goal from the pattern: 2. Any other goal: 1. Pressers: goal 2, regain in our half 1.

Progressions:
- Mirror on the right: GK → 6 → bounce to the RCB → 10 → RW.
- If their 8 does not jump, the 6 is free: he receives side-on and plays forward himself.
- Pressers free to choose who to press: we read the free man.

Dose:
3 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
12 · FULLBACK UNDERLAP
RCB → RB → RW → 10 →
RB in behind →
cutback.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Our 2-3-2-3 in position, ball with the right centre-back. Mannequins as their left midfielder, a central midfielder, their left-back and a centre-back.
- 8-10 reps on the right, then mirror on the left.

What happens:
RCB → RB → RW (wide) → 10 (inside) → RB underlaps into the half-space → cutback.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Our fullbacks start inside, in the first midfield line. When the ball goes wide to the winger, the fullback can attack the half-space from inside, where nobody tracks him.

items.text:
1 · RB INSIDE
RCB plays into the
right-back in the
midfield line.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — 1 · RCB to the RB inside
steps.note:
What happens:
The right-back stands inside, in the first midfield line. The right centre-back plays into him.

Coaching points:
- The RB receives side-on, facing up the line: he sees the winger and the 10 without turning.
- Two touches: open up with the first, pass with the second.

items.text:
2 · PASS AND GO
RB to RW, then sprints
inside the left-back.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — 2 · Wide to the winger, the RB goes
steps.note:
What happens:
The right-back plays wide to the winger and runs at once into the right half-space, inside the opposing left-back.

Coaching points:
- Pass and go: the run is the point of the pattern.
- The winger holds the width so the opposing left-back stays wide with him.

items.text:
3 · SET INSIDE
RW sets first time to
the 10. The RB keeps
running.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — 3 · Winger finds the 10 inside
steps.note:
What happens:
The winger sets the ball first time, back inside on an angle, to the 10 in the half-space. The 10 receives facing forward and sees the runner. Their midfielder has to choose: the 10 or the runner.

Coaching points:
- The winger’s set is a V: in from the right-back, back inside to the 10.
- The 10 receives facing forward, already seeing the runner.
- If nobody tracks the right-back, the next pass is on.

items.text:
4 · IN BEHIND
The 10 plays the RB
through the channel.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — 4 · Through to the underlapping RB
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 plays through into the right-back’s path, between the opposing left-back and centre-back.

Coaching points:
- Pass into space, ahead of the runner.
- The winger stays wide to keep their left-back outside.

items.text:
5 · CUTBACK
9 near post, 8 penalty
spot, LW far post.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — 5 · Cutback
steps.note:
What happens:
The right-back drives to the byline and cuts back. The 9 attacks the near post, the 8 arrives at the penalty spot, the LW attacks the far post.

Coaching points:
- Cut back behind the defenders running towards their goal.
- Three arrivals: near post, penalty spot, far post.

items.text:
PROGRESS
Live defenders · if
the RB is tracked, the
10 turns · mirror
left.

steps.title: 12 Pattern · Fullback underlap — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The fullback starts inside: from there his run is never tracked.
- Pass and go, at once.
- The winger’s width keeps their fullback outside.
- The 10 receives seeing the runner: one touch if possible.

Progressions:
- Live opponents: their left-back, left midfielder and a centre-back.
- If the left midfielder tracks the RB, the 10, already facing forward, plays the 9.
- Mirror on the left: LB underlaps, the 8 plays him through.

Dose:
8-10 reps each side, then 3 x 5 min opposed.

items.text:
13 · 9 DROPS AND SETS
6 → 9 (drops) → 8
(facing) → 10 runs
between the
centre-backs.

steps.title: 13 Pattern · 9 drops and sets — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Our 2-3-2-3 in position, ball with the 6. Mannequins as their two centre-backs and two holding midfielders. Full-size goal and goalkeeper.
- 8-10 reps, alternating which side the through ball goes.

What happens:
The 9 drops off the centre-backs into the space behind their holding midfielders, the 6 plays into him through their gap, he sets first time back on an angle to the 8 facing forward, the 10 runs between the centre-backs, the 8 plays him through.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
When the opponent’s midfield is set, our 9 comes short to create the “up” pass, and the 8 and 10 attack the space he left.

items.text:
1 · UP
The 9 drops
between the lines;
the 6 plays into
his feet.

steps.title: 13 Pattern · 9 drops and sets — 1 · The 9 drops, the 6 plays in
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 drops off the centre-backs into the space behind their two holding midfielders. The 6 plays into his feet through the gap between them.

Coaching points:
- The 9 drops when the 6 has his head up, not before.
- He shows between the lines with his back to goal: he will set, not turn.
- The 6’s pass goes through the gap between the holding midfielders, firm, to the 9’s back foot.

items.text:
2 · BACK
First-time set to
the 8. The 10 runs
now.

steps.title: 13 Pattern · 9 drops and sets — 2 · Set to the 8
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 sets first time, back on an angle, to the 8, who arrives facing forward. The 10 starts his run as the set pass travels.

Coaching points:
- First-time set: the 9 never turns into the centre-backs. The shape is a V: in from the 6, back to the 8.
- The 8 arrives from behind the ball, so he faces forward as he receives.
- The 10 runs as the ball travels to the 8, not after the 8 receives.

items.text:
3 · THROUGH
The 8 plays the 10
between the
centre-backs.

steps.title: 13 Pattern · 9 drops and sets — 3 · Through between the centre-backs
steps.note:
What happens:
The 8 plays through between the two centre-backs into the 10’s path. The 9 spins to follow for the rebound.

Coaching points:
- Through pass into space, between the centre-backs.
- The 9 spins outside his marker to arrive for a rebound or cutback.

items.text:
4 · FINISH
Early, low, across
the goalkeeper.
The 9 follows in.

steps.title: 13 Pattern · 9 drops and sets — 4 · Finish
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 finishes early, low across the goalkeeper. The 9 follows in.

Coaching points:
- Finish with the first or second touch.
- Low and across the goalkeeper.

items.text:
PROGRESS
Live defenders ·
if the 9 is
tracked, play the
10 direct ·
alternate runners.

steps.title: 13 Pattern · 9 drops and sets — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The 9 drops late and sets first time.
- Up to the man who can set, back to the man facing, through into the run.
- Runs between centre-backs start as the set pass travels.
- The 9 spins after the set: he is the second runner.

Progressions:
- Live centre-backs and holding midfielders.
- If a holding midfielder tracks the 9, the 6 plays the 10 directly.
- Alternate: the 8 runs, the 10 receives the set.

Dose:
8-10 reps, then 3 x 5 min opposed.

items.text:
14 · ISOLATE THE WINGER
Circulate left,
switch, 1v1 on the
right, cutback.

steps.title: 14 Pattern · Isolate the winger — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Our 2-3-2-3 in position, ball with the left-back. Mannequins form a block shifted to our left. One live defender: their left-back against our right winger.
- 6-8 reps. Rest 30 s between reps.

What happens:
Circulate on the left (LB → LW, set back to the LB, LB → 8, set to the 6), switch to the right winger, 1v1 against the live fullback, cutback.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Our wingers stay wide and high on the far side. We draw the block with four or five players, then switch to the 1v1.

items.text:
1 · DRAW
Four passes on the
left. RW stays wide.

steps.title: 14 Pattern · Isolate the winger — 1 · Circulate on the left
steps.note:
What happens:
Four quick passes on the left draw the block across: LB up the line to the LW, who sets first time back to the LB; LB into the 8, who sets first time to the 6.

Coaching points:
- Short and sharp: make the left look like the attack.
- The receivers with their backs to play (LW, 8) set first time on an angle; the LB and the 6 receive facing forward.
- The 6 takes the set from the 8 already facing the right: the switch needs no turn.
- The right winger stays wide and high, away from the ball.

items.text:
2 · SWITCH
The 6 finds the right
winger.

steps.title: 14 Pattern · Isolate the winger — 2 · Switch
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 received the set from the 8 already facing the right, so he switches at once to the right winger, driven to his far foot.

Coaching points:
- The 6 received from the 8 facing the right: he sees the right winger on his first look.
- Driven pass, in the air if needed, to the far foot.

items.text:
3 · 1v1
At the defender,
change pace, past him.

steps.title: 14 Pattern · Isolate the winger — 3 · 1v1
steps.note:
What happens:
The fullback comes out to the winger. The winger attacks him at speed and goes past on the outside.

Coaching points:
- First touch at the defender, inviting him to commit.
- Change of pace past his front foot.
- The right-back supports underneath in case the winger needs to recycle.

items.text:
4 · CUTBACK
9 near post, 10
penalty spot, LW far
post, 8 the edge.

steps.title: 14 Pattern · Isolate the winger — 4 · Cutback and arrivals
steps.note:
What happens:
The winger cuts back. The 9 attacks the near post, the 10 the penalty spot, the left winger the far post, the 8 the edge of the box.

Coaching points:
- Cutback along the ground behind the retreating defenders.
- Four arrival points, four players: nobody in the same lane.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A recovering defender,
RB overlaps · mirror
left · live block.

steps.title: 14 Pattern · Isolate the winger — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Draw before you switch: four passes on one side.
- The far winger is patient: wide, high, never coming to the ball.
- The switch goes to the far foot with pace.
- 1v1: attack the front foot, change pace.
- Arrivals in four different lanes.

Progressions:
- A second defender recovers after the switch: 1v1 becomes 1v2, so the right-back overlaps for a 2v2.
- Mirror on the left.
- Live block of six instead of mannequins.

Dose:
6-8 reps each side, then 3 x 5 min opposed.

items.text:
15 · v 4-4-2 HIGH PRESS
GK + 7 build
against six
pressers. Into the
end zone.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Our half plus 10 m, full width, with a 12 m end zone (orange). Blue: GK, LCB, RCB, LB, 6, RB, 8 and 10 build; LW, 9 and RW wait in the end zone.
- Red press in a 4-4-2: two strikers and four midfielders. 3 bouts of 6 minutes, 2 minutes rest. Every attack restarts from our goalkeeper.

Rules:
- Blue score by passing into a teammate in the end zone or dribbling into it under control.
- Red win it: they attack our goal; the end-zone players may not help defend.
- Normal touches. Offside line: the end zone line.

Scoring:
- Blue: into the end zone 1 point; into the end zone after a bait (a presser committed to the man on the ball) 2 points.
- Red: goal 2 points; regain in our third 1 point.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Against a front two we build with three: the goalkeeper and both centre-backs. The 6 and the inside fullbacks give the second line. Someone is always free.

items.text:
WHO IS FREE?
GK + 2 against
their front two:
one of us is
always free.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — The press: who is free?
steps.note:
What happens:
Their strikers press our centre-backs, one curving to block the goalkeeper; their midfield four push onto our 6, the fullbacks and the 8. Count: GK + 2 against 2 at the back.

Coaching points:
- Three against two: one of the goalkeeper, LCB and RCB is always free.
- Find which of our midfield players their midfield has left.

items.text:
1 · BAIT
GK to LCB. The
first striker
jumps.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — 1 · Bait with the LCB
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper plays to the left centre-back, who stops the ball. The first striker jumps him; the second striker has to choose between the 6 and the right centre-back.

Coaching points:
- LCB invites the striker, ball under the sole, body open.
- The 6 drifts away from the second striker so he cannot cover both the 6 and the RCB.

items.text:
2 · TO THE FREE MAN
LCB → GK → RCB,
the man their
press left.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — 2 · Back to the goalkeeper, out to the RCB
steps.note:
What happens:
The second striker stayed on the 6. The left centre-back plays back to the goalkeeper, who finds the right centre-back, now free.

Coaching points:
- The back pass is a forward move: it takes the ball to the free man.
- Goalkeeper: open body, play the RCB on his far foot so he can carry.

items.text:
3 · CARRY
The RCB carries;
their midfielder
must step out.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — 3 · RCB carries, their midfielder must step
steps.note:
What happens:
The right centre-back carries the ball forward. Their right-sided central midfielder has to step out to stop him, leaving the 10 free behind him.

Coaching points:
- Carry until someone stops you: the carry is how we fix a midfielder.
- The 10 stays behind the midfielder who will step, ready to show.

items.text:
4 · BEHIND HIM
The 10 is free
behind the
midfielder who
stepped.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — 4 · Into the 10 behind him
steps.note:
What happens:
The midfielder stepped, so the 10 is free behind him in the right half-space. The right centre-back plays into him.

Coaching points:
- Pass as the midfielder commits, not after.
- The 10 receives on the half-turn, already facing the end zone.

items.text:
5 · 2 POINTS
Free on the half-
turn, the 10 finds
the winger in the
end zone.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — 5 · Into the end zone: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The midfielder who stepped is behind him and nobody else is near, so the 10 receives on the half-turn, across his body, and plays the right winger running into the end zone. A bait started the move: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- First touch forward, second touch the pass.
- Winger runs into the end zone as the 10 turns, not before.

items.text:
GO OVER
Every short option
marked: long to
the 9, support the
second ball.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — If everything is marked: go over
steps.note:
What happens:
If their press covers every short option, the goalkeeper plays long, in the air over their midfield, to the 9. The 8 and 10 arrive around him for the second ball.

Coaching points:
- A controlled long pass is part of the plan, not a failure.
- Second-ball support: the 8 and 10 move under the landing point before it lands.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A seventh presser
· 8 seconds to the
end zone · man-to-
man midfield.

steps.title: 15 Phase · Build-up v 4-4-2 high press — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Count: goalkeeper plus two against their front two. One of us is free.
- Bait one presser, find the man he left.
- Carry to fix a midfielder, then play behind him.
- Through, around or over: the quickest safe exit.
- Every pass is on the far foot of the receiver.

Questions to ask:
- When their striker curved his run, which pass did he block?
- Who was free when the midfielder stepped out?

Progressions:
- Red add a seventh presser (their 10).
- Blue limited to 8 seconds to reach the end zone.
- Red press man to man in midfield.

Regressions:
- Red strikers passive on the goalkeeper.
- Five red pressers.

Dose:
3 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
16 · v 4-3-3 PRESS
Their wingers jump
our centre-backs:
the fullbacks are
free.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Same area as exercise 15: our half plus 10 m, 12 m end zone. Blue build with GK + 7; LW, 9, RW wait in the end zone.
- Red press in a 4-3-3: three forwards, three midfielders marking our 6, 8 and 10, and their left-back, who may push up onto our right-back.
- 3 bouts of 6 minutes, 2 minutes rest.

Rules:
- As exercise 15. Red midfielders follow their man (man-oriented).

Scoring:
- Blue: into the end zone 1 point; through a fullback who was freed by their winger jumping: 2 points.
- Red: goal 2 points; regain in our third 1 point.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Against a front three, their wingers jump our centre-backs. That leaves our inside fullbacks free, and their fullbacks a long way to come.

items.text:
1 · THEIR WINGER JUMPS
GK to RCB. Their
winger presses
from the inside.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — 1 · GK to RCB: their winger jumps
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper plays to the right centre-back, who stands wide at the edge of the box, side-on, facing up the pitch. Their left winger jumps him from the inside, curving so his shadow blocks the pass back to the goalkeeper and into the 6.

Coaching points:
- RCB: wide, side-on, already facing the right-back before the ball arrives.
- The right-back stays slightly deeper and outside the winger’s run, so the winger cannot cover him.

items.text:
2 · AROUND
The winger jumped:
the right-back is
free.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — 2 · The right-back is free
steps.note:
What happens:
The winger came from the inside, so the right-back is free outside him. The right centre-back is side-on and already facing him, so he needs no turn: he plays around the press with his first or second touch.

Coaching points:
- Pass as the winger commits.
- Side-on before the ball arrives: the pass to the right-back goes the way the RCB is already facing.
- The right-back receives side-on, facing up the line, seeing the right winger and the 10.

items.text:
3 · BEHIND THE FULLBACK
Their left-back
jumps; our winger
runs into the
space behind.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — 3 · Their fullback jumps: the winger is free behind
steps.note:
What happens:
Their left-back pushes up to press our right-back, coming from the inside to stop him playing into the 10. The space behind him opens: our right winger attacks it and the right-back, facing up the line, plays it down the outside.

Coaching points:
- The right winger runs as their fullback commits, not before.
- If their fullback stays, the right-back carries forward instead.

items.text:
4 · 2 POINTS
Freed fullback,
ball in behind,
end zone reached.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — 4 · Into the end zone: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The right winger collects in the end zone: 2 points, because the fullback was freed by their winger jumping.

Coaching points:
- The pass is down the line, ahead of the winger, away from the recovering fullback.

items.text:
UP AND BACK
The 8 drags his
marker; LCB → 8 →
set to the 6
facing forward.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — Alternative · Man-marking: up to the 8, set to the 6
steps.note:
What happens:
Their midfielders follow our players. The 8 drops towards the ball and drags his marker with him. The left centre-back plays into the 8, who has a man on his back, so he sets first time, back on an angle, to the 6. The 6 now faces forward, with the 8’s marker and the 8 out of the left half-space.

Coaching points:
- Use their man-marking: move to make space for someone else.
- A man on your back: set first time on an angle, never turn.
- The 6 moves as the first pass travels so the set reaches him facing forward. Next: into the space the 8 left, or a switch.

items.text:
PROGRESS
Fullbacks press at
once · striker
marks the 6 · two
touches.

steps.title: 16 Phase · Build-up v 4-3-3 press — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- When their winger jumps a centre-back from the inside, the fullback is free.
- When their fullback jumps our fullback, the winger is free behind.
- Man-marking: move to create space for a teammate; the dropping player sets, the facing player plays.
- Receive on the half-turn; the next pass is decided before the ball arrives.

Progressions:
- Their fullbacks may press immediately.
- Their striker man-marks the 6.
- Blue limited to two touches in our third.

Regressions:
- Red midfielders zonal instead of man-oriented.

Dose:
3 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
17 · v 4-4-2 MID-BLOCK
Move the block,
find the 8 or 10
between the
lines.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- From our 30 m line to their goal, full width. Blue: our 10 outfield players in the 2-3-2-3. Red: a 4-4-2 mid-block and goalkeeper.
- Two mini-goals on our 30 m line for red counter-attacks. 3 bouts of 6 minutes, 2 minutes rest. Restart from our centre-backs.

Rules:
- Normal rules, offside on.
- Red win it: they counter into either mini-goal.

Scoring:
- Blue: goal 1; goal after a receipt between the lines facing forward 2; goal within 10 seconds of a switch to an isolated winger 2.
- Red: mini-goal 1.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Against a settled mid-block our 8 and 10 must receive between the lines. We move the block with circulation and find them through it.

items.text:
1 · MOVE THE BLOCK
LCB → 6 → RCB.
Their block
slides across.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — 1 · Circulate: move the block
steps.note:
What happens:
LCB to the 6, the 6 to the RCB. Their block slides to its left to follow the ball.

Coaching points:
- Each pass to the far foot, so the next pass is quicker.
- Look forward after every reception: is the lane into the 10 open yet?

items.text:
2 · FIND THE GAP
The block
shifted: the 10
moves between
their lines.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — 2 · The 10 moves into the gap
steps.note:
What happens:
Their midfielders slid across, so a gap opens between the two midfielders on our right. The 10 moves through it, into the space between their midfield and back lines.

Coaching points:
- Receivers move into gaps late, as the block finishes its shift.
- Behind their midfield, never level with it: between the lines.
- Half-turned, showing for the pass on the outside foot.

items.text:
3 · BETWEEN THE LINES
RCB plays the
vertical pass
into the 10.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — 3 · Vertical pass between the lines
steps.note:
What happens:
The right centre-back plays the vertical pass through the gap into the 10, between their midfield and back lines.

Coaching points:
- Firm, along the ground, through the gap, into the 10’s outside foot.
- The 9 and right winger hold their positions to keep the back four deep, so the space between the lines stays big.

items.text:
4 · TURN AND THROUGH
The 10 turns;
the 9 runs into
the channel.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — 4 · Turn and play through
steps.note:
What happens:
Their left-back is 10 m away and nobody is tight behind the 10, so he receives on the half-turn, across his body, facing forward. The 9 runs across their centre-back into the channel; the 10 plays him through.

Coaching points:
- Scan before receiving: nobody behind you, receive across the body and play forward; a man on your back, set first time on an angle.
- The 9 runs across the defender, from inside to the channel, timed with the 10’s turn.

items.text:
5 · 2 POINTS
Goal after a
receipt between
the lines.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — 5 · Finish: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 finishes. Goal after a receipt between the lines facing forward: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- Finish early, near post or across the goalkeeper.
- The 8 and the left winger arrive for the rebound.

items.text:
PROGRESS
A 4-5-1 block ·
12 seconds after
the vertical
pass · full-size
counter goal.

steps.title: 17 Phase · Middle third v 4-4-2 mid-block — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Patience: circulate until the block shifts.
- Receivers between the lines move late, into gaps, half-turned.
- Vertical passes are firm and to the outside foot.
- Turn if nobody is behind you; set if someone is.
- The front three pin the back four so the space between the lines stays big.

Progressions:
- Red play a 4-5-1 (more bodies in midfield).
- Blue must score within 12 seconds of the vertical pass.
- Red counters into a full-size goal with a goalkeeper.

Regressions:
- Red midfield passive for the first two minutes.

Dose:
3 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
18 · FINAL THIRD
Pin with the front
three, attack the
channels with the
8 and 10.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- The final 47 m, full width. Blue: LB, 6, RB, 8, 10, LW, 9, RW. Red: back four, two holding midfielders, goalkeeper.
- 3 bouts of 6 minutes, 2 minutes rest. Restart from the 6 on the 58 m line.

Rules:
- Offside on. Red win it: they score by dribbling over the 58 m line or passing to a coach standing on it.

Scoring:
- Blue: goal 1; goal from a cutback 2; goal from a run into the channel between fullback and centre-back 2.
- Red: escape over the line 1.

What happens:
6 → LW, their right-back steps out, the LW sets first time back to the LB, the 8 runs into the channel, the LB plays him in, cutback.

Link to our 2-3-2-3:
Our wingers pin their fullbacks, the 9 pins both centre-backs, and the 8 and 10 attack the channels between fullback and centre-back.

items.text:
PIN
Wingers wide and
high, the 9
between the
centre-backs.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — Pin the back four
steps.note:
What happens:
The wingers hold the touchline, the 9 sits between the centre-backs. Their back four is stretched: each defender has someone to watch.

Coaching points:
- Wingers: chalk on the boots, as high as the last defender.
- The 9 stands between the centre-backs, never on one of them.

items.text:
1 · OUT TO THE WINGER
Their right-back
steps out to him.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — 1 · 6 to the left winger
steps.note:
What happens:
The 6 plays out to the left winger’s feet. Their right-back steps out to him. The left-back steps up behind the winger to give him the set.

Coaching points:
- Pass to the outside foot so the winger can protect the ball.
- The LB moves as the ball travels: inside and behind the winger, on an angle.
- The 8 watches the gap opening between their right-back and centre-back.

items.text:
2 · SET AND GO
The winger sets
back to the LB;
the 8 runs into
the gap.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — 2 · Set back to the LB, the 8 goes
steps.note:
What happens:
The right-back is on the winger’s back, so the winger does not turn: he sets first time, back on an angle, to the left-back. As the set travels, the 8 starts his run into the channel the right-back left.

Coaching points:
- A man on your back: set first time on an angle. The shape is a V: in from the 6, back to the LB.
- The run starts as the set is played, not when the LB has the ball.
- The 8 runs between their right-back and centre-back, on the blind side of the centre-back.

items.text:
3 · INTO THE CHANNEL
The LB, facing
forward, plays the
8 in behind.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — 3 · LB plays the 8 into the channel
steps.note:
What happens:
The left-back receives facing forward and plays the 8 into the channel, between their right-back and centre-back, ahead of him.

Coaching points:
- Facing forward, the third man plays first time if he can: the run is already going.
- Into space, ahead of the runner, on the side away from the centre-back.

items.text:
4 · CUTBACK · 2 POINTS
9 near post, 10
penalty spot, RW
far post.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — 4 · Cutback: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
The 8 is in behind. Their centre-backs have run back towards their goal, so the 8 cuts back behind them: the 9 attacks the near post, the 10 arrives at the penalty spot, the right winger attacks the far post.

Coaching points:
- Cut back behind the defenders running towards their goal.
- Three runners, three lanes, all arriving at speed.

items.text:
SWITCH
Left side closed:
the right winger
1v1.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — If the left is closed: switch to the 1v1
steps.note:
What happens:
If their right side is crowded, the 10 switches to the right winger, who is alone against their left-back.

Coaching points:
- Switch quickly while their back four is still shifted.
- The winger attacks his defender at once; the 9 and 8 fill the box.

items.text:
PROGRESS
Their wingers
track back · 15
seconds · channels
and cutbacks only.

steps.title: 18 Phase · Final third — Coaching points and progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Pin: wingers wide and high, the 9 between the centre-backs.
- The winger with a man on his back sets first time on an angle; the facing player plays the runner.
- Attack the channel the fullback leaves when he steps out.
- Cut back, do not cross high, when defenders are running towards their goal.
- Arrivals: near post, penalty spot, far post, edge of the box.

Progressions:
- Add their two wingers to track back (red 8 + GK).
- Blue must score within 15 seconds.
- Goals count only from the channels or a cutback.

Regressions:
- Red holding midfielders passive.

Dose:
3 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
19 · REST DEFENCE & COUNTER-PRESS
Attack with a 2
+ 3 behind the
ball. Lose it:
win it back in 5
seconds.

steps.title: 19 Game · Rest defence & counter-press — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 80 m from their goal, full width, two mini-goals on our end line. Blue: our 10 outfield players. Red: goalkeeper, back four, two holding midfielders and two strikers who stay high.
- 3 bouts of 7 minutes, 2 minutes rest. Restart from our 6.

Rules:
